Subject: Quick question on Helix-8B variant — KV cache and prompt migration

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the latency looks great. We're preparing to switch a portion of our traffic to the new Helix-8B variant you proposed. Two immediate questions from our SRE/security teams before we move forward: 

- Does Helix-8B change the KV cache semantics or prompt tokenization in a way that requires prompt migration or re-embedding of cached conversation prefixes?
- If a regression appears after rollout, can Redwood pin the session to the older Helix-8B-v1 variant (or the legacy Helix-7.x) automatically while we roll back? We need an automatic toggle we can coordinate with you so our end-users don't see hallucination/regression spikes.

I've attached our short security questionnaire and a sample convo that showed divergence in an internal test. Happy to pair up on a short call if it's easier.

Sabrina

From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Quick question on Helix-8B variant — KV cache and prompt migration

Hi Sabrina — thanks for sending this along and for the clear examples.

Short answers up front:
- KV/cache: Helix-8B introduces a spacing-change in packed KV frame headers for long-prefix caching that can cause off-by-one slice alignment in some micro-batching paths. That has caused subtle divergence in 2 of our internal test suites when combined with certain tokenizer edge-cases.
- Pin/toggle: Yes — we have a runtime fallback mechanism that can route traffic to a pinned variant during a canary or after a regression alert, but it needs two things from us to be safe: (1) a compatibility shim in the serving runtime to normalize KV frames between variants, or (2) a rollout constraint that keeps sessions pinned for the duration of a conversation.

I'm looping in Dev and Grace from infra/product to validate the impact and propose a temporary mitigation. I also attached our internal compatibility matrix (Helix-8B rows) to show where we've seen misalignment.

Action items I'm proposing here:
- Dev: confirm how much engineering effort the shim requires and whether it can be toggled per-variant.
- Grace/Product: suggest an onboarding constraint we can expose to customers (session pin TTL, auto-fallback thresholds).
- Sabrina: can you share the sampling rate for traffic you plan to shift? That helps estimate risk.

Aditya
Aditya Rao
Head of Product — Redwood Inference

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compatibility gap: toggle fallback and onboarding constraints for Helix-8B variant

Thanks for the context — I dug into the runtime traces and kernel dispatch. Summary:

- Root cause: Helix-8B changes the token packing length for long prefixes (a minor protobuf framing change in the export). The serving runtime's fast-path assumes identical frame lengths between warm cache entries and live generation. When packing differs, we end up with shifted KV offsets and misapplied cached keys for ~0.2% of requests in our stress tests.
- Mitigation options:
  1) Compatibility shim: runtime-level translator that normalizes legacy frames to the new shape on read. Estimated 3–4 engineer-weeks including tests and a feature flag. Safe to toggle per-variant.
  2) Session pin TTL: expose a customer-level option (e.g., pin sessions to variant for N hours) and add auto-unpin after N tokens. Low effort (1 engineer-week) but doesn't fix already-warmed caches across variant transitions.
  3) Canary + auto-fallback: keep current canary, add an SLO-based trigger to fallback routing to previous variant when divergence > X% on our eval set. Medium effort (2 weeks) because we need a quick eval harness and routing guardrails.

My recommendation: short-term, surface a pin TTL to Acuity and run a focused fix for the shim as a medium-term project (feature-flagged). That gives customers an immediate, low-risk lever while we eliminate the root cause.

I'll start a PR with unit tests and a feature-flag flow if you want — ETA for a candidate branch would be ~3 weeks.

—Dev
Dev Patel
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime — Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>

Date: Mon, 22 Jun 2026 10:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Compatibility gap: toggle fallback and onboarding constraints for Helix-8B variant

Adding product perspective. We need two customer-facing controls for this:

1) "session_variant_ttl": a per-tenant config we expose in the model config UI/API (default 2 hours, configurable 0.5–24h). That prevents mid-conversation variant flips. Low risk to implement and we can document it as part of onboarding.

2) "auto_fallback_threshold": an SLO-driven toggle (percent of eval prompts with regressions over a 5m window). If exceeded, routing automatically keys to the previous pinned variant for new sessions. We'll need SRE runbooks for noisy signals.

For onboarding language: recommend we mark Helix-8B as "experimental" in the model catalog for 2 weeks and require opt-in via the tenant config. That gives customers like Acuity an explicit opt-in while we ship the shim.

I'll draft the onboarding blurb and a short FAQ for customers. Laura — can you sign off on comms and any contract implications?

—Grace
Grace O'Connor
Product Manager, Redwood Inference

Commitments from Redwood:
- Short-term: expose "session_variant_ttl" (product/API) and document experimental flag in the model catalog — Grace to draft and ship a tenant-facing FAQ by EOD Wed (2026-06-24).
- Short-term: enable canary + auto-fallback guardrails and add Acuity as a monitored canary customer (Dev to stand up eval hooks) — ETA for initial routing guard is 2 weeks; I'll surface progress bi-weekly.
- Medium-term: Dev to implement compatibility shim behind a feature flag to normalize KV frames — target branch in ~3 weeks.
- Redwood will add an explicit pin/unpin API endpoint so partners can programmatically request re-routing for live sessions during incidents.

Sabrina — can you confirm the sampling % you want for the initial canary (1%, 5%, 10%) and whether Acuity would like the session_variant_ttl default to 4 hours instead of our proposed 2? Also confirm if your security team needs anything else from the questionnaire.

Thanks,
